Subject: Ops acceptance checklist for reserved GPU reservation

Hi Priya — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick written recap so we have a single source of truth and clear handoff to ops/infra teams. I’ve summarized the pain, goals, and the items we agreed to validate before the reservation move to purchase.

Summary of pain and goals
- Production latency spikes at 95th percentile during nightly batch transformations (current infra: mixed CPU/generic GPU).
- Model serving tail latency and cache pressure are causing timeouts for interactive clinical QA flows.
- Goal: stable 95p latency <= 350ms for standard chat endpoints, and sustained throughput for batch inference windows with predictable cost.
- Must have tenant isolation for PHI routing and SOC 2 audit evidence for separation.

What we agreed to validate (ops acceptance checklist)
1) Isolation scope: dedicate a reserved GPU pool per environment (staging/prod) with tenant VLANs and KMS-backed keys for model artifacts.
2) Throughput targets: baseline throughput of 600 reqs/min with autoscale headroom to 2x during peak bursts.
3) Latency SLO: 95th <= 350ms for 2k token average sequences (we'll validate against your 1k/2k prompt mix).
4) Fallback policy: automatic routing to an elastic shared fallback model when reserved pool utilization exceeds 85%.
5) Audit evidence: exportable audit logs (token-level metrics redacted for PHI) and SOC 2 checklist entries.
6) Network policy: egress restrictions and the VPC peering diagram you shared (see attachment).

Next steps / owners
- Alex (me): deliver the ops acceptance checklist + proposed reserved pool sizing by EOD tomorrow (attached spreadsheet).
- Rishi: run a quick throughput simulation against a quantized variant for cost estimate; outcome by Friday.
- Priya: confirm the batch window schedule and provide a sample 24-hour traffic histogram (CSV) so we can calibrate burst slots.

Attachments: OPS_ACCEPTANCE_CHECKLIST.xlsx (spreadsheet with validation rows), orion-network-topology.pdf

If this matches your understanding I’ll start the sizing work and loop in our private deployment lead for the IAM/KMS validation.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

Alex — this is excellent, thanks for capturing. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing:

- Batch windows: primary nightly window is 02:00–05:00 UTC, with ad hoc daytime batches from 17:00–18:00 UTC. I’ll attach the histogram (coming separately).
- PHI isolation: critical that the reserve pool prevents any cross-tenant memory reuse; our compliance team flagged GPU memory wiping and per-job encryption keys as must-haves.
- Fallback behavior: acceptable as long as the fallback model is constrained to non-PHI traffic.

We can confirm the sample traffic by EOD Thursday. Also, we have a procurement constraint: any dedicated contract must include a 30-day SLA ramp clause and an option to increase reserved capacity in 90-day increments without a full renegotiation.

Looking forward to the sizing sheet.

—Priya
